sourceArticle.title: A satellite just learned to find things on its own — here’s what that means
sourceArticle.author: Tim Fernholz

athenaOutput.directive: Adopt the 'Orbital Autonomy' paradigm: Transform the Creative Liberation Engine's agents into Sovereign Creative Satellites—un-tethered, artist-owned edge nodes that independently forage for inspiration, protect IP, and generate value without relying on centralized ground control or constant human prompting.
athenaOutput.rationale: A satellite learning to find things on its own represents the ultimate shift from centralized command-and-control to autonomous edge intelligence. For the Creative Liberation Engine, this means moving beyond the 'prompt-response' loop. If we deploy agents that can autonomously observe, decide, and act at the edge, we fulfill Article I (Sovereignty) by breaking reliance on big-tech cloud orchestration, and Article XX (Zero human wait time) by allowing the system to work continuously and unprompted on the artist's behalf.

options.title: Sovereign Edge Node Architecture (The 'Orbital' Engine)
options.description: Restructure the Creative Liberation Engine so that individual agent hives can be deployed as completely isolated, self-sufficient nodes (satellites) on local hardware. These nodes autonomously scan predefined cultural or data inputs, making creative decisions and generating assets without pinging a central server.
options.tradeoffs: Requires significant upfront architectural work to ensure nodes are truly independent (Article XXIII) and can handle local compute constraints, but delivers absolute sovereignty and resilience.

options.title: Autonomous Inspiration Foragers
options.description: Deploy 'scout' agents that act like observation satellites. They continuously orbit the digital landscape (social feeds, open-source repos, design networks), autonomously identifying emerging aesthetic patterns and depositing them into KEEPER as a curated, evolving mood board for the artist.
options.tradeoffs: Risk of accumulating 'data junk' or noise requiring periodic human pruning, versus the massive benefit of a constantly replenishing, unprompted well of inspiration.

options.title: Orbital IP Defense Grid
options.description: Utilize autonomous observation to protect artist rights. Deploy a swarm of lightweight, read-only agents that continuously scan the web for unauthorized use of the artist's visual DNA or biometric data (Article XXIV), automatically drafting takedowns via LEX.
options.tradeoffs: High risk of false positives that could lead to aggressive automated actions; requires strict 'human-in-the-loop' for the final execution phase, balancing automation with legal safety.

options.title: Zero-Prompt Generative Streams (Experiential)
options.description: Create an always-on experiential art installation where an autonomous AI satellite ingests real-world telemetry (weather patterns, network traffic, satellite imagery) and translates it into a continuous, evolving visual narrative without any human intervention.
options.tradeoffs: Sacrifices direct, granular artistic control for pure, continuous autonomous expression; highly resource-intensive to run continuously.

options.title: Decentralized Compute Scavengers
options.description: If a satellite can find targets, an agent can find compute. Develop an autonomous system that scours a decentralized, sovereign network for available, low-cost GPU cycles, routing rendering and model-inference tasks dynamically to bypass centralized cloud providers.
options.tradeoffs: Introduces unpredictable latency and potential security vulnerabilities during data transit, but drastically reduces reliance on AWS/GCP/Azure.

options.title: Cloud-Tethered 'Dumb' Terminals
options.description: Maintain a centralized AI architecture where the 'satellite' is merely a sensor that streams all raw data back to a proprietary, closed-source cloud LLM for processing and decision-making.
options.tradeoffs: Easy to implement and highly performant, but completely violates Article I (Sovereignty), Article XXIII (LLMs are components, not architecture), and Article XXIV (Biometric Data Sovereignty).
